title: An In-Memory Computing Accelerator with Reconfigurable Dataflow for Multi-Scale Vision Transformer with Hybrid Topology
problem: Vision Transformers require substantial computational and storage resources due to lack of inductive bias, hindering deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Existing accelerators for hybrid MHA-CNN models optimize either convolution or attention at the expense of flexibility.
motivation: Hybrid transformer-CNN models offer promise for computer vision but need efficient hardware acceleration to enable practical edge deployment.
method: The accelerator employs SRAM-based digital in-memory computing macros to mitigate memory access bottlenecks while avoiding analog non-ideality. It introduces pipeline reordering and provides reconfigurable processing engines and interconnections to flexibly map both convolution and multi-head attention operations.
key_novelty: Digital SRAM-based in-memory computing architecture with reconfigurable dataflow enabling efficient acceleration of both convolution and multi-head attention in hybrid vision transformers.
contributions: SRAM-based digital IMC macro architecture supporting hybrid MHA and convolution topology
Pipeline reordering technique for improved efficiency
Reconfigurable processing engines and interconnections for flexible workload mapping
Demonstration of 2.20×-2.52× speedup and 40.6%-74.8% energy reduction
limitations: Scalability to larger models, thermal considerations, and comparison with emerging technologies not discussed.
primary_theme: reconfigurable in-memory computing for hybrid vision transformers
